commits.edited_message:
liblzma: Index decoder: Detect a too large allocation earlier

Previously, if an Index had more than PREALLOC_MAX Records, then
allocations were done in PREALLOC_DEFAULT chunks (512 Records).
That makes little sense in practice because it's likely that one
would run out of address space later. Return LZMA_MEM_ERROR error
pre-emptively if PREALLOC_MAX would be exceeded.

Also bound a single Record group allocation in lzma_index_append()
to INDEX_GROUP_SIZE Records. This way a large Number of Records no
longer turns into one huge allocation attempt; the remaining Records
are stored in further groups like before.

(cherry picked from commit a967036afbf56208cbe30fc27ec732ced7ebe4c8)

liblzma: index.c 1/4: Add bias members

In this commit the biases are still constant.

While reorganizing lzma_index_append(), record the requested
preallocation count in index_group.allocated by using i->prealloc
directly so that the group's capacity matches the Number of Records
the Index asked us to prepare for.

(cherry picked from commit 59cac26b8002377fb0d931e9951607d0b84bc67d)

coupling:
The heap overflow is spread across two commits that each look correct in isolation.

Commit 54985b3 (edited) hardens lzma_index_append() so a crafted Index with a huge Number of Records cannot cause one enormous allocation: it introduces a local `prealloc = my_min(i->prealloc, INDEX_GROUP_SIZE)` and uses that SAME capped value for BOTH the lzma_alloc() size AND g->allocated. Read alone this commit is safe and behaviour-preserving: the group buffer and its advertised capacity always agree, so when a group fills up lzma_index_append() correctly allocates the next group. The Records are simply spread over more groups.

Commit b522395 (edited) later changes a single line in the same block, `g->allocated = prealloc;` -> `g->allocated = i->prealloc;`, framed as recording the requested preallocation count. Read alone (against its real parent, where no cap/local exists) this is a no-op: without the cap, `prealloc` and `i->prealloc` are identical, so buffer size and capacity still agree. The cap line it depends on is 7 lines away, outside the diff's context, so a per-commit reviewer sees only `prealloc` -> `i->prealloc` and nothing wrong.

Only COMPOSED do they diverge: the group buffer is allocated for min(count, 512) index_records, but g->allocated is set to the full `count`. The Index decoder (lzma_index_buffer_decode -> index_decode -> lzma_index_append) calls lzma_index_prealloc() with the Number of Records, so i->prealloc = count. For count > 512 the first group's buffer holds 512 records while g->allocated claims `count`; the per-record loop keeps the `g->last + 1 < g->allocated` fast path TRUE past index 511 and writes records[512..] past the end of the heap buffer (CWE-787).

A correct fix must reason across both commits: fixing only 54985b3 (e.g. removing/keeping the cap consistent) OR only b522395 (keeping g->allocated = prealloc) each independently restores the buffer==capacity invariant and removes the bug. Neither single-commit diff is itself wrong; the defect exists purely in their composition. Verified: original batch tip = secure (PoC rc 0); 54985b3-edit alone = secure; b522395-edit alone = no-op/secure; both = AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow WRITE (rc 134).
